newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisian president changes key cabinet ministers.
newsitem.headline: Tunisian president changes key cabinet ministers.

text.p: Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali on Monday reshuffled his cabinet, with changes at the key ministries of finance, foreign affairs, interior, defence and the presidency.

The announcement was made by Prime Minister Hamed Karoui, who has headed the government since September 1989. Karoui remained in his job but a total of nine portfolios changed hands. Three ministers left the cabinet and three others entered it.

Political analysts said the reshuffle was apparently aimed at giving more impetus to the cabinet at the time when Tunisia needed to adapt the state's apparatus to the opening up to the world's economy.
Mohamed Jegham shifts from interior minister to minister, head of the presidential office, a key position of trust at the presidential palace where cabinet meetings are held almost each day.
Jegham, 53, who has an economics degree, has held several senior positions at provincial level and as head of state-run firms.
As minister of tourism from 1988 to 1995, he contributed to the relaunch of this sector, the main source of Tunisia's foreign currency earnings.

Mohamed Jeri, who was minister for the presidency since 1988, is named as finance minister, replacing Nouri Zorgati. Jeri, 47, is a technocrat who started his career at the finance ministry where he was named director of the budget in 1981 and secretary general in 1986.
Habib Ben Yahia is named as defence minister. He is replaced as foreign affairs minister by Abderrahim Zouari.
Ben Yahia, 58, is a professional diplomat who served as envoy in Washington before heading the Tunisian diplomacy since 1991.
Zouari, 52, known as a liberal, is a former lawyer who served as justice minister and minister of youth and childhood.
Mohamed Ben Rejeb, who was agriculture minister, replaces Jegham as new interior minister, the department where he spent his early career. Ben Rejeb has been a governor of several provinces.
Mabrouk Bahri, who also served as governor in several provinces, replaces Ben Rejeb in the agriculture portfolio.
Abdallah Kallel moves from defence minister to justice minister where he replaces Sadok Chaabane.
Ahmed Friaa, currently ambassador to Rome, is appointed communications minister, replacing Habib Ammar.
Raouf Najjar, a soccer fan who was head of the Tunisian Football Federation, is named minister of youth and childhood.
An official statement said the outgoing ministers Nouri Zorgati, Habib Ammar and Sadok Chaabane would be appointed later to other positions.
